title: Backtracking
summary: Try, recurse, undo: the shape behind puzzles and solvers.

cards.title: Choose, explore, un-choose
cards.body: Backtracking builds a solution step by step. At each step it tries a choice, goes deeper, and if that leads nowhere it **undoes** the choice and tries the next. Sudoku solvers, puzzle generators and level validators work this way.
Red = undo. Try n = 6 in the Algorithm Lab: many more dead ends.
The `colOf[row] = -1` line is the whole technique: restore the state exactly as it was before trying.

cards.question: Why check only rows ABOVE the current one in `safe()`?
choices: Rows below are empty: we fill one row at a time
cards.explain: Queens are placed top to bottom, so only earlier rows contain queens.
